comment: Recall at top-k over a symbol queried by its own doc comment, on real code in this repository.
**The query set was written by the authors of the code, not by a reviewer.** A doc comment describes the
symbol that follows it, so the expected answer is read off the file rather than chosen - which is what "no recorded
**Comments that name their own symbol are excluded**, because those are lexical lookups wearing the clothes
of a description. What remains is the size of this measurement, and it is smaller on purpose.
**The semantic half is reported only with a backend named**, because the embedding backend here is
intermittent: one probe threw `Tokenizer not found` and later runs report `onnx`.

backend.note: the first figure is BM25 alone; the second had vectors registered on the same engine

withVectorsRegistered.note: only meaningful when `backend` is not `none` - with no embedder this is the lexical figure again

andWhyThereIsNoModel.reading: **The package declares that it ships `models/` and ships none.** 32 KB is a source package; a bundled ONNX model with its tokenizer is two orders of magnitude larger. **So `createFromPackage` fails every time it is called, and always has.**

andTheEmbedderIsNotIntermittentItIsAbsen.andTheSourceAlreadySaidSo: `embed.ts` carries a comment saying exactly this - "the package declares `files: ['dist', 'models']` and ships no `models/`, so `createFromPackage()` cannot find it". **The code was right and three rounds of documentation were wrong**: they called the result *intermittent*, which is what a swallowed error looks like from outside.
andTheEmbedderIsNotIntermittentItIsAbsen.andItIsNotFixableFromHere: **Installing the model needs the model.** It is not in the package, it is not in this repository, and fetching it needs network access this environment does not have. **So the semantic half of the search row is blocked on an artefact rather than on work** - and `embedderUnavailableReason()` now says so in one sentence.

theFamilyWasCounted.method: Every TypeScript file under `packages/*/src` that is not a test, scanned for a `catch` whose only statement is a return of a plausible-looking value - `null`, `[]`, `{}`, `''`, `false`, `undefined`. **That is the static projection of a failure that cannot be told from success.**

andTheClassificationMattersMoreThanTheCo.optionalDependencyProbes: **Thirteen of the twenty.** `loadBetterSqlite3`, `brotliCompressSync`, `project-detector`'s filesystem checks, `agent-setup`'s absent config: **the catch is asking whether an optional thing is present**, and returning `false` or `null` is exactly the answer to that question. **These are correct.**
andTheClassificationMattersMoreThanTheCo.absenceIsTheAnswer: **Four more.** A cache path that does not exist, a session file that is not there, a webhook secret that is unset: **the caller is asking whether something exists**, and `null` is the true answer rather than a swallowed failure.
andTheClassificationMattersMoreThanTheCo.emptyResultVersusFailure: **The three worth looking at.** `fetchPRFiles`, `discoverRelatedRepos` and `findReposConsumingSymbol` **return `[]` when a network call or an index lookup fails**, and the caller cannot distinguish *"there are none"* from *"it could not be determined". **That is the same ambiguity as the four confirmed members of this family, in a smaller form.**

theFamilyWasCounted.andThisIsNotTwentyDefects: **A count from a regex is not a finding and this records it as a count.** The precedent in this repository is that reading these sites settles most of them: an earlier pass over thirty-seven `catch` blocks that return a value found eight of eight deliberate across two shapes. **What the scan is good for is narrowing twenty sites to the three that need a reader.**

andTheThreeHaveNoCallers.finding: **All three functions have zero references outside their own declaration**, including from tests: `discoverRelatedRepos`, `findReposConsumingSymbol` and `fetchPRFiles` are never called.
andTheThreeHaveNoCallers.andThatReordersTheWork: The ambiguity the previous round fixed a symptom of **cannot reach anybody**: a caller cannot be misled by an empty list it never receives. **The larger fact is that these three are not wired to anything**, which is a different question with a different next step - **connect or remove, rather than make the failure describe itself.**
andTheThreeHaveNoCallers.andItMatchesSomethingAlreadyKnown: A previous pass on this repository found three feature flags in the ablation runner that were never connected. **Same shape: the capability is written and nothing calls it.** That is now two occurrences of a pattern worth looking for deliberately - **not "does this work" but "is this reached".**
andTheThreeHaveNoCallers.andItIsWhyReportingFirstWasRight: **The reporting step found the wiring problem.** Had the fix gone straight to changing three return types, every caller would have been updated - **of which there are none** - and this would still not have been noticed.

andTheReachabilityCheckWasWrittenAndWron.whatWasAsked: **Not "does this work" but "is this reached"** - the question no test asks, because a test calls the thing it tests. Every exported top-level function and method across four packages, counted for calls anywhere in the tree **including tests**.
andTheReachabilityCheckWasWrittenAndWron.andTheFirstNamesCheckedWereWrong:
`checkNoEvalAst`, `checkNoXssAst`, `checkNoUndef` and a dozen more appeared in the list, and they are **live rule implementations**. They are reached through a registry:

    rule-runner.ts:1817    'no-undef': checkNoUndef,
    rule-runner.ts:1827    'no-eval': astChecker(checkNoEvalAst),

**Neither line has parentheses after the name.** The scan counted `name(` and a function passed as a value has none - **so it reported live code as unreachable.**
andTheReachabilityCheckWasWrittenAndWron.andThatIsTheEleventhTime: **The scan answered a nearby question - "is this name followed by a parenthesis" - and the question asked was "is this reached".** `checkNoEvalAst` is reached by being mentioned in a table; **no regex over call syntax can see a value being passed.**
andTheReachabilityCheckWasWrittenAndWron.andSoTheNumberIsNotReported: **72 is a property of the check and not of the code, so it is recorded here as wrong rather than published.** Roughly forty of the seventy-two are rule functions in two registries, which alone puts the true figure far below it. **Reporting it would have been a number that looked like a finding.**
andTheReachabilityCheckWasWrittenAndWron.andTheRightInstrumentIsTheProductItself: **A reference analysis is what `code-analyzer` does**: it builds a symbol graph and resolves references across files. **This check was written with a regular expression while the tool that answers it properly was in the same repository** - and it is the reason the number is wrong.

andTheIndexCannotAnswerItYet.whyWeAskedTheIndex: The previous round ended with *"ask the index instead of the text"* - a reference analysis is what this product does, so the count should come from it rather than from a regex.
andTheIndexCannotAnswerItYet.andThatIsTheFinding: **`CALLS` is in the relationship vocabulary and no edge of that type is ever produced.** Every edge in this graph is structural - *defines*, *is a member of*, *has a method*, *contains* - and **none of them is a call.** So the index cannot answer *"is this reached"* either: **the reachability question needs a call graph and there is not one.**
andItIsTheSixthOfItsFamily: **the parse fallback** returned regex output on every grammar error
**three functions** were written, tested and never called
andTheIndexCannotAnswerItYet.andWhatItCosts: **Impact analysis, dead-code detection and reachability all need call edges**, and the regular-expression reachability count was written because there was no alternative. **That is the same shape as the doc-comment scan being written because the field was empty** - the instrument gets worse when the thing it should use is missing, and **the workaround then looks like a choice rather than a consequence.**

andMyProbeWasWrongThreeTimesGettingHere.note: **The field list was printed only on the third attempt**, after two reads of a field that does not exist. Both wrong answers read "0 edges of type CALLS", which is **the correct reading of a wrong question** - and **the first thing to do with an unfamiliar record is print its keys.**
andMyProbeWasWrongThreeTimesGettingHere.andItIsTheTwelfthAndThirteenthTime: The same defect twice inside one probe: a check that could not answer the question asked. **The count of those in this stretch is now thirteen**, and this one was caught by printing the record rather than reasoning about it - **which is the cheapest method available and was used third.**
